# ankra_host_join_token (Resource)

A single-use token that lets a host register into a deploy environment, for example from a machine's cloud-init (`ankra targets register --environment <environment> --name <name> --token-stdin`). The counterpart of `ankra targets join-token create`. The environment is created in the provider's project when it does not exist yet.

The platform shows the token once and keeps only its hash: there is no read-back and no revoke. Terraform keeps the token in state until it is destroyed, which removes it from state only; the token itself stays valid until it is used or `expires_at` passes. An expired token is not re-minted automatically: replace it (`terraform apply -replace`) when a new host needs one. Registering the host and revoking a host target are host-side operations and are not managed here.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "ankra_host_join_token" "kiosk" {
  environment = "edge"
  ttl_seconds = 3600
}

# Hand the token to the host's first boot, for example from cloud-init:
#   echo "$JOIN_TOKEN" | ankra targets register --environment edge --name kiosk-1 --token-stdin
output "kiosk_join_token" {
  value     = ankra_host_join_token.kiosk.join_token
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `environment` (String) Environment the host registers into: lower-case letters, digits and `-`, at most 63 characters. Changing it mints a new token.

### Optional

- `ttl_seconds` (Number) Token lifetime in seconds, 1 to 86400. Unset takes the platform's one-hour default. Changing it mints a new token.

### Read-Only

- `expires_at` (String) When the token stops being accepted (RFC 3339).
- `id` (String) `<environment>/<expires_at>`, unique per minted token.
- `join_token` (String, Sensitive) The join token. Shown by the platform only once.
